{{ElectionsCA}}
An election will be held in the U.S. state of California on November 3, 2026, to elect the next [[governor of California]]. The nominees are [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former secretary of health and human services [[Xavier Becerra]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] political commentator [[Steve Hilton]]. Democratic incumbent [[Gavin Newsom]] is [[Term limits in the United States|ineligible]] to seek re-election to a third term.

The statewide [[Nonpartisan primary|top-two primary election]] was held on June 2, 2026, with Becerra and Hilton advancing to the general election among the 61 candidates on the ballot.<ref name="Certified List">{{cite web|url=https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/statewide-elections/2026-primary/cert-list-candidates.pdf|title=Certified List of Candidates for June 2, 2026, Primary Election|website=[[Secretary of State of California]]|date=March 26, 2026}}</ref> Republicans have not won a gubernatorial race in California since [[2006 California gubernatorial election|2006]].

==Primary election==
===Campaign===
Sixty-one candidates qualified for the primary ballot. California uses a [[Nonpartisan primary|top-two primary]] system in which all candidates, regardless of party, appear on the same ballot, with the top two advancing to the general election.<ref name="Segura 2026">{{Cite news |last=Segura |first=Daniella |date=April 3, 2026 |title=California governor primary guide with candidates dates, voting info |url=https://www.desertsun.com/story/news/nation/california/2026/04/03/california-governor-primary-election-guide-2026/89409390007/ |access-date=April 11, 2026 |work=[[The Desert Sun]]}}</ref>

Among Republicans, [[Riverside County Sheriff's Department|Riverside County sheriff]] [[Chad Bianco]] and political commentator [[Steve Hilton]] emerged as the leading candidates, while the Democratic field remained fragmented. This raised concerns that two Republicans could advance to the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2025/12/26/californias-very-odd-election-year-starts-with-republicans-possibly-leading-the-governors-race/|title=California's very odd election year starts with Republicans possibly leading the governor's race|last=Walters|first=Dan|work=[[The Orange County Register]]|language=en-US|date=December 26, 2025|access-date=January 12, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Politico 2026">{{Cite web |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/09/californias-governor-race-mess-00817776 |title=8 Democrats and no front-runner: California's governor race is a mess |language=en |date=2026-03-09 |access-date=2026-03-11|website=Politico}}</ref> Those concerns eased after President [[Donald Trump]] endorsed Hilton, increasing the chance of a Democrat making it into the runoff because some Bianco supporters would likely shift their support to Hilton due to Trump's endorsement.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Collins |first=Terry |date=April 10, 2026 |title=Trump endorsed former Fox host. It could tip balance in this CA race. |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2026/04/10/trump-endorsement-steve-hilton-california-governor/89498710007/ |access-date=April 11, 2026 |work=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

Before Swalwell's exit from the race, polls showed that the three Democrats with the greatest amount of public support were representative [[Eric Swalwell]], hedge fund manager and [[Tom Steyer 2020 presidential campaign|2020 presidential candidate]] [[Tom Steyer]], and former representative [[Katie Porter]].<ref name="Politico 2026" /> Other notable Democrats running included former [[mayor of Los Angeles]] [[Antonio Villaraigosa]], former HHS Secretary and [[California Attorney General|state attorney general]] [[Xavier Becerra]], [[Mayor of San Jose, California|mayor of San Jose]] [[Matt Mahan]], and [[California State Superintendent of Public Instruction|superintendent of public instruction]] [[Tony Thurmond]].<ref name="Segura 2026" /> Former Vice President [[Kamala Harris]] and U.S. Sen. [[Alex Padilla]] opted against running for governor, despite speculation by the media to the contrary.<ref name="Politico 2026" />

====Eric Swalwell sexual assault allegations====
{{Main|Eric Swalwell#Sexual assault allegations}}

On April 10, 2026, the ''[[San Francisco Chronicle]]'' reported allegations from a former staffer who provided credible claims that Swalwell had sexually assaulted her on two occasions.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Koseff |first1=Akexei |last2=Bollag |first2=Sophia |date=April 10, 2026 |title=Ex-staffer says Eric Swalwell, candidate for California governor, sexually assaulted her |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/politics/article/eric-swalwell-allegations-22198271.php |access-date=April 11, 2026 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]}}</ref> That same day, [[CNN]] published additional claims from four women, including one allegation of rape and others describing inappropriate conduct and unsolicited nude photos. CNN reported that it had corroborated the accounts. Swalwell denied all of the allegations and sent cease-and-desist letters to two of the women threatening legal action.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Gordon |first1=Allison |last2=Chapman |first2=Isabelle |last3=Tolan |first3=Casey |last4=Brown |first4=Pamela |author-link4=Pamela Brown (journalist) |date=April 10, 2026 |title=Exclusive: Four women describe sexual misconduct by Rep. Eric Swalwell, including a former staffer who says he raped her |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/04/10/us/eric-swalwell-sexual-misconduct-allegations-invs |access-date=April 11, 2026 |work=[[CNN]]}}</ref>

Following the allegations, several staff members resigned from Eric Swalwell's campaign, including co-chairs [[Jimmy Gomez]] and [[Adam Gray]].<ref name="Rosenhall 2026">{{Cite news |last=Rosenhall |first=Laurel |date=April 10, 2026 |title=Swalwell Faces Sex Assault Accusation as He Runs for California Governor |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/10/us/politics/eric-swalwell-allegations-california-governor.html |access-date=April 11, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref><ref name="Mueller 2026">{{Cite news |last1=Mueller |first1=Julia |last2=Vakil |first2=Caroline |date=April 10, 2026 |title=Swalwell loses campaign chairs, endorsements over sexual assault allegations |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5826574-swalwell-loses-campaign-chair-endorsements-over-sexual-assault-allegations/ |access-date=April 11, 2026 |work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]}}</ref> The [[California Teachers Association]] revoked its endorsement,<ref name="Rosenhall 2026" /> while U.S. Senators [[Adam Schiff]] and [[Ruben Gallego]] also withdrew their support.<ref name="Mueller 2026" /> House Minority Leader [[Hakeem Jeffries]] and former Speaker of the House [[Nancy Pelosi]] called on Swalwell to end his campaign.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/04/10/eric-swalwell-house-democrats-00867951|title=Jeffries, Pelosi and other Democrats call on Eric Swalwell to end governor campaign|date=April 10, 2026|website=Politico|last=Rogerson|first=Riley}}</ref> By April 11, all of Swalwell's 21 fellow members of Congress previously endorsing him had withdrawn their support.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solender |first=Andrew |date=2026-04-11 |title=Eric Swalwell loses all 21 of his endorsements from Democratic colleagues in Congress |url=https://www.axios.com/2026/04/11/eric-swalwell-endorsements-sexual-misconduct |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref> The following day, he announced that he was suspending his campaign for governor.<ref>{{cite web | title=Eric Swalwell drops bid for California governor after sexual misconduct allegations | website=[[NBC News]] | date=April 13, 2026 | url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/eric-swalwell-drops-bid-california-governor-sexual-misconduct-allegati-rcna277009 }}</ref> On April 13, Swalwell announced he had plans to resign from Congress,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Swalwell |first=Eric |date=April 13, 2026 |title=Rep. Eric Swalwell Announces Resignation Plans |url=https://x.com/RepSwalwell/status/2043802702971359521 |website=X.com}}</ref> and formally left on April 14.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-14 |title=Reps. Eric Swalwell and Tony Gonzales officially resign amid misconduct claims |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/reps-tony-gonzales-eric-swalwell-officially-resign-misconduct-claims-rcna331765 |access-date=2026-04-14 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref>

====Canceled debate====
A debate scheduled for March 24, 2026, hosted by the [[USC Center for the Political Future]], [[KABC-TV]], and [[KMEX-DT]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Debate for California Governor Includes CPF and ABC7|url=https://dornsife.usc.edu/center-for-political-future/news/california-governor-debate-2026/|date=March 14, 2026| publisher=[[USC Center for the Political Future]]}}</ref> was ultimately canceled hours before it was set to begin.<ref name="Austin 2026">{{cite news|title=University cancels California governor debate after accusations of bias from candidates of color|url=https://apnews.com/article/california-governor-debate-usc-candidates-bias-91539c81a8ecaf8612c0eacd04dc1312|first=Sophie|last=Austin|date=March 26, 2026| publisher=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Using a formula developed by USC political science professor [[Christian R. Grose]] that combined fundraising and polling data, only six candidates were invited: Republicans Bianco and Hilton, and Democrats Mahan, Porter, Steyer, and Swalwell.<ref>{{cite news|title=USC cancels California governor debate after excluding candidates of color|url=https://www.sfgate.com/politics/article/usc-cancels-california-gov-debate-22093688.php|first=Anabel|last=Sosa|date=March 26, 2026| publisher=[[SFGate]]}}</ref> The selection drew criticism from chairs of the black and Latino caucuses, particularly because no nonwhite candidates qualified and because Mahan's strong fundraising offset weaker polling. USC and over 50 scholars defended the formula, but the debate was canceled after organizers could not agree to expand the field.<ref name="Austin 2026" />
